items.fullText: 전국 스마트큐브 '큐브 트윈', 日 전시회서 주목기술 2위…산업용 AI에이전트 시장 공략 발행일 : 2026-11-22 09:30 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 일본 '넥스테크 위크 도쿄 투 2026 오텀' 전시회 부스. 산업용 인공지능(AI) 에이전트 선도기업 스마트큐브(대표 임지숙)는 자사 디지털트윈 플랫폼 '큐브 트윈(CUBE-TWIN)'이 지난 11~13일 열린 일본 '넥스테크 위크 도쿄 투 2026 오텀' 확장현실(XR) 산업활용전의 공식 제품 검색 사이트에서 주목 기술 2위에 올랐다고 22일 밝혔다. 이 순위는 지난 16일 기준 제품 검색 사이트의 조회 수를 바탕으로 집계된 것으로, 전시 개최 전부터 스마트큐브의 산업현장 적용 기술과 솔루션에 대한 잠재 참관객들의 관심을 확인했다는 점에서 의미가 있다. 스마트큐브는 이번 전시회에서 제조·에너지·물류 분야의 주요 기술과 구축사례를 소개하고, 일본 현지 제조기업 및 스마트팩토리·시스템 통합(SI). 디지털 전환(DX) 관련 기업과의 사업협력 가능성을 모색했다. 이 회사는 산업별 특화 AI에이전트를 디지털트윈 엔진 기반의 직관적인 인터페이스로 제공하는 산업 지능화 기술을 핵심 사업으로 추진하고 있다. CUBE-TWIN은 프로그래머블 로직 컨트롤러(PLC)·센서·제조실행시스템(MES)·전사적자원관리시스템(ERP) 등 산업 데이터를 실시간으로 연계하고 3차원(3D) 가시화와 시뮬레이션으로 설비 운영 상태를 모니터링하는 플랫폼이다. AI 기반 이상탐지·예지보전·공정 최적화로 기능을 확장할 수 있으며, 우수 소프트웨어(GS) 인증 1등급을 획득해 제품 신뢰성도 확보했다. 주요 구축사례로는 △전주·완주 수소 메가스테이션 통합관제 △대구경 강관 제조공정 실시간 모니터링 △컴퓨터 수치 제어(CNC) 공작기계 설비 상태 분석 △부산항 물류 차량 및 컨테이너 이동경로 추적 등이 있다. 이러한 산업현장 구축 경험을 바탕으로 데이터 분석·예측과 의사결정을 지원하는 산업별 특화 AI에이전트 기술도 고도화하고 있다. 스마트큐브는 올해 일본 삿포로에 설립한 현지법인을 기반으로 현지 기업과의 기술협력과 실증사업(PoC) 등 사업 기회를 넓혀갈 계획이다. 내년 1월 열리는 'CES 2027'에서 산업별 특화 AI에이전트와 AI 코파일럿, 디지털휴먼 기술을 결합한 차세대 플랫폼 'CUBE-TWIN 3.0'을 선보일 예정이다. 임지숙 대표는 “이번 도쿄 전시회는 스마트큐브의 산업용 AI 기술력을 일본시장에 알리고 현지 기업과의 협력 가능성을 모색한 뜻깊은 기회였다”며 “산업별 특화 AI에이전트 기술을 고도화하고 일본 현지법인을 기반으로 글로벌 시장 진출을 확대해 나가겠다”고 말했다. 전남광주=김한식 기자 hskim@etnews.com

items.fullText: 경제 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 "배보다 배꼽이 더 클 판"…서학개미 200만원 벌고 '날벼락' [고정삼의 절세GPT] 입력 2026.11.21 07:30 수정 2026.11.21 08:02 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 고정삼 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 연말정산 꿀팁 정당 후원금 등 회사에 알리기 싫은 공제 항목 이듬해 5월 종합소득세 신고 때 직접 반영 가능 교육비·기부금 등 최근 5년간 경정청구로 환급 해외주식 매매차익 100만원 초과시 부양가족 탈락 사진=챗GPT 생성 이미지 <고정삼의 절세GPT>에서는 독자들이 궁금해할 세금 관련 이슈를 세법에 근거해 설명합니다. 38회는 송주영 유안타증권 세무전문위원과 함께 연말정산을 앞둔 직장인이 자칫 놓치기 쉬운 사항들에 대해 알아봅니다. 직장인이 고대하는 '13월의 월급' 연말정산 시기가 다가오고 있다. 세금을 한 푼이라도 더 돌려받으려면 놓치기 쉬운 공제 항목과 요건을 꼼꼼히 살펴봐야 한다는 게 전문가의 조언이다. 21일 세무업계에 따르면 연말정산은 1년간 납부한 세금과 실제 내야 할 세금을 비교해 차액을 환급받거나 추가 납부하는 과정으로, 직장인 사이에서 흔히 '13월의 월급'으로 불린다. 문제는 연말정산을 회사가 알아서 처리해주는 절차로 여기는 직장인이 많다는 점이다. 우선 회사에 알리고 싶지 않은 공제 항목은 연말정산에서 제외하고 이듬해 5월 종합소득세 신고 때 직접 반영할 수 있다는 점을 염두에 둘 필요가 있다는 게 세무사의 조언이다. 정당에 후원한 정치자금과 종교단체 기부금, 난임부부 시술비 등 민감한 개인정보가 포함된 항목이 대표적인 예다. 회사에 관련 증빙 자료를 제출하지 않아도 공제 혜택을 받을 수 있기 때문이다. 송주영 유안타증권 세무전문위원은 "연말정산을 위해 자신의 사생활까지 회사에 공개해야 하는 것은 아니다"며 "민감한 정보와 관련된 공제 항목은 회사 연말정산에서 제외하고 이듬해 5월 직접 신고하는 방법을 활용할 수 있다"고 설명했다. 과거에 놓친 공제 항목도 다시 들여다볼 필요가 있다. 법정 요건을 충족했으나 공제받지 못한 항목은 원칙적으로 법정 신고기한이 지난 후 5년 안에 경정청구를 통해 환급 신청할 수 있기 때문이다. 경정청구는 납세자가 과다 납부한 세금의 환급을 요구하는 절차다. 대표적으로 교육비와 의료비, 기부금, 부양가족 관련 공제 등을 청구할 수 있다. 국세청 간소화 서비스에서 조회되지 않는 자료도 살펴봐야 한다. 대학원 등록금과 초등학교 취학 전 자녀의 학원비, 중·고등학생 자녀의 교복·안경 구입비 등이 해당한다. 간소화 서비스에 나오지 않더라도 세법상 공제 요건을 충족하고 증빙 자료를 갖추면 공제받을 수 있다. 송 세무전문위원은 "간소화 서비스에 나오지 않는다고 해서 공제받을 수 없는 게 아니다"며 "과거 5년간 연말정산 내역을 다시 확인해 교육비와 기부금, 부양가족 등 누락 항목이 있다면 경정청구를 적극 활용할 필요가 있다"고 조언했다. 특히 부양가족의 해외주식 투자 수익을 확인할 필요가 있다. 배우자와 부모, 자녀 등을 기본공제 대상자로 올리려면 원칙적으로 연간 소득이 100만원 이하여야 한다. 근로소득만 있을 경우 총급여 500만원 이하의 별도 기준이 적용된다. 문제는 해외주식 매매차익이 100만원을 초과하면 부양가족 기본공제 대상에서 제외된다는 점이다. 해외주식은 연간 매매차익에서 250만원을 기본공제하기 때문에 양도소득세가 발생하지 않을 수 있으나 부양가족 공제 기준은 이와 달라서다. 불이익은 기본공제에 그치지 않는다. 해당 가족의 신용카드 사용액과 보험료, 교육비, 기부금 등에 대한 공제도 제한될 수 있다. 예를 들어 미성년 자녀가 해외주식을 매도해 150만원의 매매차익을

items.d: A bruising stock market sell-off continued despite a record-setting IPO by Anthropic, dashing hopes it would revive sentiment on the AI trade.
items.fullText: Markets Markets plunge: Nasdaq erases 2026 gains, S&P and Dow enter corrections Anthropic’s record-setting IPO Thursday failed to restore investor confidence in the AI market. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Stock markets plunge as Nasdaq erases 2026 gains 01:54 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 20, 2026, 9:20 AM EST / Updated Nov. 20, 2026, 4:37 PM EST By Rob Wile The surging stock market of 2026 capsized Friday, wiping out gains for the year in the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite while the broad S&P 500 and the Dow entered correction territory, meaning they have declined 10% from recent peaks. The dramatic sell-off is raising fresh fears about the viability of the AI investment wave that had powered stocks and economic growth for the first half of the year. Friday’s declines were led by Anthropic, whose blockbuster IPO just 24 hours earlier now feels like a blip after the stock lost 9%, wiping out hundreds of billions in paper wealth and putting shares just a few dollars above the IPO price. Nvidia also dragged markets lower, tumbling about 14% following a Reuters report that regulators are looking into accounting irregularities at the chip giant. With Friday’s losses of 3.7%, the S&P 500’s seven-day losing streak is its worst since the Covid pandemic; the index is now up less than 1% on the year. The Nasdaq finished the day down 5.3%, and the Dow dropped 1.9%. The losses also sully one of the most visible bright points of President Donald Trump’s second term. Amid sticky inflation and frozen housing and jobs markets, U.S. equities were the one part of the economy that appeared resilient. The AI investment boom created seemingly insatiable demand for stocks among investors, minting multiple new trillion-dollar companies in the process. Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Physical AI Paves the Path to Autonomous Industrial Operations 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Nyhamna_footage_take5_30s.mp4 AI agents powered by frontier models pave the way to autonomous operations. They use industrial tools and engineering data to help engineers build digital twins that test plans and processes and evaluate operational decisions. Falkor, a KONGSBERG company, shows how this works in practice. The company’s Falkor Surface platform lets customers turn their computer-aided design and engineering data into facility-scale digital twins using the GPT-6 Astra model. The platform uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition GPUs on Microsoft Azure to enable advanced physics simulation. items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Another AI company is about to be worth more than $1 trillion. What that means for the rest of us. Anthropic’s public market debut comes as the AI investment boom stands at a crossroads. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Anthropic co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei in Washington, in September. Finn Gomez / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 18, 2026, 4:13 PM EST / Updated Nov. 18, 2026, 4:23 PM EST By Rob Wile Leading AI lab Anthropic is expected to make the largest-ever public market debut when it starts trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange Thursday. Founded in 2021 by brother and sister Dario and Daniela Amodei, both former employees of rival OpenAI, Anthropic and its main product, Claude, are seen as the gold standard of AI models, despite lacking the household name cache of ChatGPT. With a target market value of $1.5 trillion — larger than SpaceX’s record setting IPO just a few months ago — Anthropic’s public arrival will serve as more than just a measure of what Wall Street thinks the company is worth. It will be a test of current sentiment around AI itself at a pivotal moment for the industry. For much of the past year, the AI investment wave has powered the stock market to new heights and sustained U.S. economic growth. But there are signs the wave may be starting to break. “Investors have over recent weeks become increasingly concerned around the sustainability of the investment boom,” James McCann, senior economist for investment strategy at Edward Jones, said in a client note Wednesday ahead of Anthropic’s debut. The market gains notched in the spring and summer thanks to the AI boom have now largely been wiped out. Fears of overspending on infrastructure, rising debt loads, ballooning costs and uncertain demand have grown. New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work. Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops. Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC. A Windows PC Built for Local AI As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks. RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system. Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks. items.fullText: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents At SC26, NVIDIA’s VP of Hyperscale and HPC laid out how researchers can combine simulation, AI and agents to accelerate scientific discovery. November 17, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. Researchers can run it locally on a DGX Spark, a workstation or their own supercomputer. In its MLPerf benchmarks debut, with results released today, the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform delivers leading performance across training, post-training and agentic inference. NVIDIA swept every MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark and, in its first MLPerf Endpoints submission, delivered more than 10x generational gains in throughput per watt for agentic AI — measuring how much agentic work a system delivers with each watt of power. These results are just the beginning. Vera Rubin performance will keep climbing through continuous optimization of NVIDIA’s CUDA-powered software stack , so the infrastructure that customers invest in today delivers more value over time. NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training v6.1 AI agents are now everywhere, writing code, running business workflows, answering customer questions and, as this week’s SC26 conference highlights , advancing scientific research. Faster training means smarter agents can reach users sooner, drug discovery models can keep pace with new lab data and fraud-detection models can adapt to new threats faster. MLPerf Training measures how fast a system can train a range of AI models to a target level of accuracy. The NVIDIA platform was the only one with results on every benchmark this round, spanning large language models, image generation, recommender systems and reinforcement learning post-training. In its debut, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered up to 2x more performance per GPU than the highly optimized NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 system — early results that show the pace of generation-over-generation innovation. items.fullText: NVIDIA CUDA-X Libraries Give Agents the Tools to Accelerate Scientific Discovery November 16, 2026 by Kibibi Moseley 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! With expanded NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, including cuPhoton, cuPotential and cuSpa, researchers can sift through vast amounts of data to accelerate research, from astrophysics and materials science to single-cell biology. The speedups are helping scientists analyze larger datasets and model more complex systems. The new libraries give AI agents the tools to help researchers make discoveries faster than ever. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Bringing Black Holes Into Focus Seeing a black hole takes a telescope the size of Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope links radio dishes worldwide, generating petabytes of data that can take months to process. With NVIDIA cuPhoton.xBeam, a module within the cuPhoton Toolkit , black hole observations from the Event Horizon Telescope can now be correlated orders of magnitude faster than ever. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes. By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution. cuPhoton successfully correlated observations of powerful black hole jets J1924 and 3C279 in the night sky — making it a reality to reconstruct a Messier 87* black hole galaxy in real time. The entire pipeline, from data loading and processing to visualization, runs on distributed multi-GPU systems or a compact NVIDIA DGX Spark system, helping scientists study how gas spirals inward under a black hole’s powerful gravitational pull. Steering Fusion Simulations Sustaining plasma at millions of degrees is essential to achieving stable, continuous fusion energy. But simulating its behavior is costly: on petascale systems, a single time step can take days, with simulations running for weeks. items.fullText: AI Day Seoul Brings Together Korea’s Industry Leaders, Startups and Developer Communities November 15, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Over two days at COEX, more than 2,000 attendees converged for AI Day Seoul, bringing together Korea’s industry leaders, startups and developer communities advancing physical AI and AI agents. At the plenary sessions, Deepu Talla, vice president of robotics and edge AI at NVIDIA, said Korea is “punching above its weight,” with Doosan Robotics, Hyundai Motor Group, LG Electronics and SK Group — as well as startups like Real World and Luda Robotics — using NVIDIA platforms to bring general-purpose robotics into the real world. Jonathan Cohen, vice president of applied research at NVIDIA, showed how enterprises can build agents they own and control. Breakout sessions featured speakers from Coupang Intelligent Cloud, Doosan Robotics, LG AI Research, LG Electronics, NAVER Cloud, SK Telecom and Upstage. “It was a genuinely enjoyable time to have candid conversations,” said Hyunho Yang, research engineer for omnimodal foundation models at SK Telecom. “Seeing the passion of fellow AI developers was a real source of inspiration for me.” Community leaders share how they build with open models and tools at AI Day Seoul. The Agentic AI 10x Bootcamp Community Day brought together Pseudo Lab, Python Korea, PyTorchKR, HAERAE, Hugging Face KREW, Graph User Group, Womxn Who Code Korea, Dnol (Datayanolja) and other developer communities. Five finalists from the Hangul Day hackathon, co-hosted with Fastcampus, built agents trained on the Korean language and culture with the OpenShell runtime. The winning team, FlyGate, received an NVIDIA DGX Spark system. More than 500 developers also took part in full-day NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute workshops and NVIDIA Certification exams in Korean.
